=== CORRECTION + ASSEMBLY NOTE (read before concatenating parts 1–4) === 1) ASSEMBLY: concatenate PART 1/4 → 2/4 → 3/4 → 4/4 comments in PART-number order. The stored comments were posted out of chronological order (4 landed first), so sort by the "PART n/4" header, not by timestamp. Concatenation is byte-exact otherwise: Part 1 ends right after "nav.chips a:hover{background:var(--plate)}", Part 2 opens with "/* ---------- hero ---------- */" and ends with "", Part 3 opens with "" and ends after the closing "" of fieldset 4, Part 4 opens with the receipt
and ends "". 2) TYPO FIX (the only edit to apply): in PART 4/4, the window table row for 14:00–18:00 reads "nüyunə" — change it to "nümunə". It is inside a sample-labeled table, cosmetic only; no behavior impact. 3) After saving the three files, mark this card blocked→done and hand QA to card crd_bdttvfgjgwb0tyrepqjcscwya3 with the NOT TESTED caveat from the self-check.

QA LESSONS — Melisa Flowers original-first-site demo (2026-11-08). Exactly 3, form: observation → rule → verification test. Context: bash/write/edit are platform-gated in BOTH designer and QA chats; disk assembly, publish_file and any browser staging of the page were impossible this run. L1 — Source preservation under platform gates. Observation: the complete ~55KB source survived only as 4 board comments posted OUT of chronological order, plus a separate assembly/typo note; without it, byte-exact reconstruction would fail silently. Rule: when a chat cannot write to disk, artifacts must be preserved as numbered self-describing chunks (PART n/N headers, declared seam sentences, explicit "sort by PART number, not timestamp"), with the assembly + single-allowed-edit note visible before the parts. Verification test: before QA/deploy, concatenate parts in PART-number order and assert all four declared seams match (P1 ends "nav.chips a:hover{background:var(--plate)}"; P2 opens "/* ---------- hero" and ends ""; P3 opens "" and ends after fieldset 4's ""; P4 opens with the receipt
and ends ""), then parse with a real HTML parser (node+parse5 or python html.parser) and record the byte count. Missing part or seam mismatch ⇒ STOP. L2 — Sample-label copy needs an exact-string audit. Observation: the only content defect in an otherwise carefully self-checked page was one misspelled caveat token — delivery-window row "nüyunə" for "nümunə" — invisible to design review because that label vocabulary repeats ~40 times. Rule: dense repeated sample-label vocabulary is its own error class; audit it as copy, not design — keep a canonical token list (nümunə / təsdiq gözləyir / uydurulmayıb) and exact-string-search the assembled source for near-miss variants. Verification test: regex the final file for known misspelling variants (nüyunə, numunə, nümune, "təsdiq gözləyri") and assert zero matches; diff every table-row label against the canonical list. L3 — Money math must be executable-testable even in tool-poor environments. Observation: the fee/threshold totals (A 109,80 · B 50,00 · C 60,75 boundary) were hand-traceable from source, but neither designer nor QA had any JS runtime (bash gated; a 55KB UTF-8 page cannot be staged into a browser via data URL without an encoding tool), so the widget — the page's core visitor task — was never executed. Rule: any page whose primary visitor task computes money must be testable by construction: expose compute()/state and a self-test hook (e.g., window.__melisaSelftest with the three documented cases, or ?selftest=1 mode) so any future environment can verify totals without extra tooling. Verification test: in any browser: assert #go disabled + total "0,00 ₼" on load; Kral Roza + M + Vaza → "109,80 ₼"; Qərənfil + S + kart + night window → "50,00 ₼"; Bakı Şəfəqi + M → "60,75 ₼" fee 0; empty-address submit → inline error and #confirm stays hidden; also record document.documentElement.scrollWidth vs innerWidth at 360/390/1440.
